item.content:encoded: NBA top 100 defenders rankings (1-10): Who is No. 2 after Victor Wembanyama in the top 10 for 2026-27? originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The league is full of brilliant defenders that never truly get their due. I've ranked them up to 100 every year in order to bring more attention to the defensive side of the ball. In Part 1 of this series, I covered some of the more underrated players that ranked from No. 11 to 100 . In Part 2, we're getting to the well-established names in the top 10. All of the players in the top 10 have the ability to swing games due to their defensive ability. Watch them closely inside of the last two minutes and you will see something special, as they take away huge portions of the floor or find ways to create game-changing turnovers. Spoiler alert: Victor Wembanyama is at No. 1 on this list and will probably hold that top spot for the next decade. The battle for No. 2 is a much more interesting question, and I have two players who have skyrocketed from last year's list that were in top consideration for that spot. Here's who I have at No. 2, along with the stalwarts that make up the rest of the top 10. Top 100 defenders of 2023-24 | Top 100 defenders of 2024-25 | Top 100 defenders of 2025-26 The best defenders in the NBA: 1-10 Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images 1. Victor Wembanyama, Spurs Wembanyama won his first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year award last season, and he should win a flurry more over the coming years. He's the most game-changing defender of his generation, and he's only getting better as a 22-year-old. Wembanyama's eight-foot wingspan allows him to do things that nobody else can. He's a blocks machine, leading the league during every season of his career thus far. He should retire as the best shot-blocker of all time. He also uses those long arms to swipe for crazy steals and pick off passes. Wemby has become synonymous with players U-turning any time they see him lurking in the paint. "You literally don't even want to go to the hole when he's on the floor," LeBron James said recently on his Mind the Game podcast. Wemby is also a capable defender on the perimeter, although the one minor area of improvement for him is to stop being so jumpy out there. He's willing to run step-for-step with Steph Curry as he wiggles through screens, and his length allows him to recover when he does get temporarily beat. Wemby's impact shows up all across the numbers. He's No. 1 in blocks per game. He's No. 1 in defensive estimated plus-minus. The Spurs defend a massive 8.7 points per 100 possessions better with him on the floor versus off. And he inherited a team that was last in the league in defense and brought them up to No. 3 last year. Any list of the best defenders has to have Wemby at No. 1. The runner-up position is where things start to get interesting. MORE: Why Victor Wembanyama earns Sporting News' Defensive Player of the Year award 2. Scottie Barnes, Raptors Barnes doesn't back down from any matchup, whether it's Wemby or Donovan Mitchell. He's by many accounts the most versatile defender in the league, able to stay in front of guards and bang down low with bigger players. Barnes is a turnover-generating machine. His 114 steals and 116 blocks made him the only player in the league to finish with over 100 in both categories, and his 230 combined "stocks" (steals + blocks) was behind only Wemby. Those weren't empty calories either. Barnes led the league with nine clutch blocks. Barnes' impact goes well beyond blocks and steals. He plays with force, gunking up what opponents are trying to do. He does his work early, refusing to cede positioning and blocking lanes to throw entry passes. He's a monster help defender, ripping the ball away whenever it's near him and switching teammates out of bad matchups. He's a great rim protector, covering a ton of ground. And when his matchup does get the ball, he makes it hell to score on him one-on-one. The Raptors are going to be an elite defense this season, and Barnes will be their anchor. RANKING ALL 150 NBA STARTERS: 11-150 | Top 10 3. Ausar Thompson, Pistons The Thompson twins are widely regarded as among the most athletic players in the league. Ausar uses those gifts to absolutely hound opponents, taking away their breathing room as soon as they step off the bus. While his athleticism generates the headlines, it's actually everything else about his defense that makes him elite. As pointed out by defensive guru Mike Jagacki , Thompson is a great fundamental defender, using both hands to contest shots. He uses his physicality to jam up ballhandlers, controlling the positioning battle. He knows how to time the ball on gathers, ripping it away for steals. And when he does get beat, he has the crazy hops to recover and block shots. Thompson's defensive skill can completely swing a playoff series. Just ask Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson, who had to gameplan around him during last year's Eastern Conference Semifinals. "The tactical adjustment we made was avoiding Thompson," Atkinson admitted after his team won in seven games. "If he's near the ball, throw it to someone else." Thompson's numbers scream off the page in the advanced statistics as well. He was the No. 2 defender in Estimated Plus-Minus (EPM), along with standing out in multiple categories on BBall Index. Ausar Thompson's perimeter defense numbers are ridiculous https://t.co/ZmrIR4K28V — BBall Index (@The_BBall_Index) December 31, 2025 Thompson and Barnes are in a tier of their own in the race for the No. 2 defender in the league. Either would be a worthy choice. 4. Alex Caruso, Thunder Caruso's fearless style doesn't allow him to play enough minutes to rank higher on this list. He is constantly throwing his body around the floor with reckless abandon, and the Thunder have to save him from himself so that they have him available for the biggest playoff games. When the postseason hits and they take the reins off, Caruso is one of the most disruptive players in the tracking era. In a 29-year sample of defensive RAPM, former NBA analytics staffer Jeremias Engelmann found that only Kevin Garnett, Dikembe Mutombo, Alonzo Mourning, and Tim Duncan ranked higher than the 6-foot-5 guard. That lack of size hasn't stopped Caruso from bothering big men like Nikola Jokic, who he famously matched up against during Game 7 of the 2025 Western Conference playoffs. And he shuts down guards routinely. Caruso is more physical than anyone, oftentimes annoying opponents and fans who aren't comfortable with his line-balancing routine. That's part of his strategy. "If I finish a game with no fouls, I probably didn’t play hard enough," Caruso admitted back in 2021 during his Bulls days. Caruso is far from just a bruiser. He takes the brunt of damage from opponents, sacrificing his body for charges, diving on the floor for loose balls, and throwing himself into moving screen-setters to force whistles. He has textbook technique for how to stay attached to opponents, making him nearly impossible to screen. Caruso is a leader, too. He's the most vocal guy on the floor, screaming out coverages and directing teammates where to go. He has an encyclopedic knowledge of playbooks across the league, which allows him to know what teams are running and where the ball is going. His combination of effort, film study, technique, and fearlessness make him the greatest guard defender in the history of the game. MORE: Alex Caruso's wild journey, from 'a nice little camp player' to NBA superstar stopper 5. Rudy Gobert, Timberwolves Gobert finished fourth in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season, which seems about right. He's won the award four times in the past, but Wemby was correct with what he said back in 2024. "[Let Gobert win] it now, because after that, it's no longer his turn." item.title: Crimson Crank: Nitpicking Indiana’s 19-15 loss to Ohio State
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Indiana Hoosiers WR Nick Marsh (11) catches what would have been a game go-ahead touchdown while stepping out of bounds during a college football game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and Indiana Hoosiers on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana suffered its first loss since 2024 on Saturday afternoon, falling to Ohio State 19-15. It was a hard-fought game between two evenly-matched teams, as reflected by the the fact that the Hoosiers fell just one spot in the latest AP Poll. Because of how winnable the game was, fans and media alike have spent much of the last two days trying to figure out who to blame, particularly for Indiana’s final offensive play. After struggling for most of the day, Josh Hoover threw a ball that was good, but not great, to Nick Marsh, who caught it with his feet out of bounds to effectively end the game. It’s a painful play to revisit, even as I sit here thinking about it Monday evening. But was that really what cost Indiana the game? Not really. I was critical of the passing game on Saturday because the accuracy issues predated the Ohio State game. Indiana punted four times, in addition to the two field goal tries, because drives kept stalling out when Hoover missed passes. Any one of these could have ended in the touchdown that would have won the game for the Hoosiers. Then there are the missed field goals. Radicic missing an easy one had an immeasurable impact on the game. Had he converted from 32 yards out, Indiana’s final drive wouldn’t have had to end with a shot at the end zone. The drive could have been planned around just getting into Radicic’s normally consistent range. It’s not fair to blame Radicic for the miss from 55-yards, but it’s another play – more so than the Hoover’s last pass – worthy of a closer look. After the Nebraska game, I questioned whether Cignetti had lost some of the aggression that made last year so special. The decision to kick down six from well beyond Radicic’s career-long only makes me worry more. Because Radicic had never really given us reason to think this was in his range, I struggle with calling this the “safe” call from Cignetti. It’s kind of just a head-scratcher. I watched Indiana’s offense on Saturday, like everyone else, so I do understand lacking confidence in execution on a crucial fourth down play. That said, there are going to be other high-leverage plays this season that the offense will need to execute on, so they may as well practice now. With how much Indiana has struggled to run the ball the last few weeks, the staff may have felt somewhat handcuffed in play-calling, which could have impacted the decision. The defense was also playing well, making a turnover feel less threatening in that scenario. Saturday’s result, though, demonstrates that offenses have to make plays to win games. item.content:encoded: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Indiana Hoosiers WR Nick Marsh (11) catches what would have been a game go-ahead touchdown while stepping out of bounds during a college football game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and Indiana Hoosiers on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana suffered its first loss since 2024 on Saturday afternoon, falling to Ohio State 19-15. It was a hard-fought game between two evenly-matched teams, as reflected by the the fact that the Hoosiers fell just one spot in the latest AP Poll. Because of how winnable the game was, fans and media alike have spent much of the last two days trying to figure out who to blame, particularly for Indiana’s final offensive play. After struggling for most of the day, Josh Hoover threw a ball that was good, but not great, to Nick Marsh, who caught it with his feet out of bounds to effectively end the game. It’s a painful play to revisit, even as I sit here thinking about it Monday evening. But was that really what cost Indiana the game? Not really. I was critical of the passing game on Saturday because the accuracy issues predated the Ohio State game. Indiana punted four times, in addition to the two field goal tries, because drives kept stalling out when Hoover missed passes. Any one of these could have ended in the touchdown that would have won the game for the Hoosiers. Then there are the missed field goals. Radicic missing an easy one had an immeasurable impact on the game. Had he converted from 32 yards out, Indiana’s final drive wouldn’t have had to end with a shot at the end zone. The drive could have been planned around just getting into Radicic’s normally consistent range. It’s not fair to blame Radicic for the miss from 55-yards, but it’s another play – more so than the Hoover’s last pass – worthy of a closer look. After the Nebraska game, I questioned whether Cignetti had lost some of the aggression that made last year so special. The decision to kick down six from well beyond Radicic’s career-long only makes me worry more. Because Radicic had never really given us reason to think this was in his range, I struggle with calling this the “safe” call from Cignetti. It’s kind of just a head-scratcher. I watched Indiana’s offense on Saturday, like everyone else, so I do understand lacking confidence in execution on a crucial fourth down play. That said, there are going to be other high-leverage plays this season that the offense will need to execute on, so they may as well practice now. With how much Indiana has struggled to run the ball the last few weeks, the staff may have felt somewhat handcuffed in play-calling, which could have impacted the decision. The defense was also playing well, making a turnover feel less threatening in that scenario. Saturday’s result, though, demonstrates that offenses have to make plays to win games. Whether it’s Hoover settling down and making passes that he’s capable of making, or Mike Shanahan retooling the run game to get Lee Beebe Jr. and Turbo Richard some better looks, it’s not a problem Indiana can shy away from. I don’t pretend to have an answer, but taking a step back from Saturday makes it clear that the loss has more to do with issues that have been plaguing Indiana’s offense well before the Buckeyes got to town. If Indiana can clean these things up and string together more scoring drives, there will be no reason to litigate single incompletions. Join the conversation! item.title: The recurring strategic mistake NFL teams continue to make
item.description: WoodysPhotos/Depositphotos 357192806 ericbvd/Depositphotos Why NFL teams struggle to build balanced rosters NFL teams often invest heavily in star players, but individual talent cannot solve every problem on a roster. Offensive-line protection, defensive depth, salary-cap limits and quarterback development all play important roles in a team’s success. Recent roster decisions involving the Detroit Lions, Houston Texans, Cleveland Browns and Dallas Cowboys highlight the challenges of building a balanced team. Ringo Chiu/Shutterstock.com Failing to protect the franchise quarterback Quarterbacks receive major contracts and often become the center of a team’s long-term plans. However, Houston’s experience entering 2026 shows why quarterback investment must be matched by reliable offensive-line protection. C.J. Stroud was sacked 90 times during his first two NFL seasons, ranking second among quarterbacks from his draft class behind Bryce Young. His sack total fell to 23 in 2025, demonstrating how changes in protection can affect a quarterback’s exposure to pressure. Depositphotos Treating offensive-line problems as temporary Offensive-line weaknesses can persist across multiple seasons when teams repeatedly replace departing starters rather than build continuity. Houston continued addressing its protection problems during the 2026 offseason, while Detroit faced challenges following major personnel losses. Detroit lost guard Kevin Zeitler in free agency and center Frank Ragnow to retirement before the 2025 season. Injuries and replacements led to frequent lineup changes, leaving the Lions with another major offensive-line priority heading into 2026. Depositphotos Giving quarterbacks a stronger supporting cast Drafting a promising quarterback does not automatically solve a franchise’s offensive problems. Young passers also benefit from effective protection, dependable receivers and clear coaching. Cleveland evaluated Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders during the 2026 offseason before naming Watson its opening-day starter on August 24. The Browns also rebuilt their offensive line through trades, free agency and the draft, showing how a quarterback decision fits into a broader effort to strengthen an offense. parasunak.yandex.ru/Depositphotos Spending heavily without accounting for depth A roster’s starting lineup does not tell the full story of its readiness for a long NFL season. Injuries, substitutions and departures can force teams to rely on less experienced players at important positions. Philadelphia entered the 2026 season with concerns about offensive line depth, including questions about players dealing with recurring injuries. NFL.com also identified depth as a concern for San Francisco’s offensive line, showing that even established contenders must plan for personnel changes beyond their starting groups. Offensive-line protection, defensive depth, salary-cap limits and quarterback development all play important roles in a team’s success. The Browns also rebuilt their offensive line through trades, free agency and the draft, showing how a quarterback decision fits into a broader effort to strengthen an offense. parasunak.yandex.ru/Depositphotos Spending heavily without accounting for depth A roster’s starting lineup does not tell the full story of its readiness for a long NFL season. Injuries, substitutions and departures can force teams to rely on less experienced players at important positions. Philadelphia entered the 2026 season with concerns about offensive line depth, including questions about players dealing with recurring injuries. NFL.com also identified depth as a concern for San Francisco’s offensive line, showing that even established contenders must plan for personnel changes beyond their starting groups. WoodysPhotos/Depositphotos Rebuilding the same position group repeatedly Repeatedly rebuilding a position group can leave teams struggling to establish consistency from one season to the next. Free agency, trades and draft selections offer solutions, but they also require teams to manage departures and replacements together. The Browns faced this challenge entering 2026 after preparing for significant changes along the offensive line. NFL.com reported that Cleveland was set to lose potentially four of its five 2025 starters, creating a substantial personnel problem alongside its unresolved quarterback situation. Ringo Chiu/Shutterstock.com Neglecting the defense while building the offense An offense filled with productive players cannot, on its own, prevent opponents from scoring. Teams must also maintain an effective pass rush, cover receivers and stop running plays to compete across a full season. The Dallas Cowboys entered 2026 with significant defensive needs after trading Micah Parsons before the 2025 season. NFL.com identified the pass rush and secondary as areas requiring attention, illustrating how losing a major defensive contributor can create multiple roster-building challenges. Interesting fact : The NFL’s salary cap topped $301.2 million for the first time in 2026. Depositphotos Building a unit takes more than one signing A prominent signing can address a clear weakness, but dependable offensive-line play requires several players working together. Teams must consider scheme fit, communication and depth alongside individual ability. Houston retained Ed Ingram and Trent Brown with contract extensions during the 2026 offseason and added other offensive linemen. Those moves formed part of a broader effort to protect C.J. Stroud and maintain continuity across the unit. Depositphotos Ignoring how injuries affect long-term plans Injuries can change a team’s priorities even when its original roster plan appears sound. Reliable backup players and flexible personnel options help teams respond when starters miss games or struggle to return to full health. Detroit used 13 offensive linemen during the 2025 season, tying for the league lead in that category. The number reflected the combined effects of roster changes and injuries, while highlighting the challenge of maintaining a consistent unit throughout an NFL campaign. Depositphotos Matching draft investments to roster needs The NFL Draft gives teams a chance to address weaknesses while developing players for the future. Combining draft selections with veteran additions can provide several ways to strengthen the same position group. Detroit addressed its offensive line by selecting Clemson tackle Blake Miller with the No. 17 pick in the 2026 draft and signing center Cade Mays in free agency. The approach combined a first-round investment with the addition of an experienced professional following significant changes to the unit. Depositphotos Balancing roster needs against the salary cap NFL teams must balance immediate improvements against the financial commitments in player contracts. Spending on one position can reduce the flexibility available to strengthen another. In a February 20, 2026, assessment, NFL.com reported that Houston was $4.7 million over its projected salary-cap limit. The Texans later extended Ed Ingram and Trent Brown, illustrating how roster planning involves both managing financial commitments and deciding which contributors to retain. herreid/Depositphotos Adapting when the original lineup changes Injuries and personnel changes can force teams to revise their plans during the season. Green Bay responded to early protection problems by adding veteran guard Laken Tomlinson and changing its starting combinations. Through Week 3, Jordan Love had taken 31 hits, and the Packers ranked 31st in pressure rate allowed at 44.7%. Their protection improved in Weeks 4–5, when Love took 7 hits and the team allowed pressure on 20.3% of dropbacks, according to an October 15 NFL.com report. The NFL playoff picture can change quickly as teams develop their strengths and capitalize on weaknesses across the league. Check out how these 6 NFL teams could shake up the Super Bowl race . thenews2.com/Depositphotos Repeating mistakes instead of building a complete roster Star players give teams an advantage, but dependable protection, defensive contributors and capable reserves help keep a season on course. Building that support requires decisions across the roster, from retaining veterans to developing draft picks and responding to injuries. Detroit’s offensive-line investments, Houston’s contract extensions and Green Bay’s adjustments show the different ways teams can respond. The challenge continues after opening day, as front offices and coaches work to keep their personnel suited to the demands of the season. Officials play a central role in maintaining order and enforcing rules during high-pressure NFL games, making disciplinary decisions a closely watched issue. item.title: Indiana’s Malia Samuels lands NIL deal with World’s Finest Chocolate
item.description: Malia Samuels. | Photo courtesy of World’s Finest Chocolate. Many college athletes view NIL deals as opportunities to support good causes. Indiana women’s basketball player Malia Samuels’ new NIL deal with World’s Finest Chocolate is one of those feel-good stories of giving back. World’s Finest Chocolate is a fundraising company that helps schools, sports teams, clubs, and community organizations raise money by giving youth the opportunity to sell chocolate. From third to fifth grade, Samuels sold WFC’s chocolate to fund travel basketball opportunities and follow her dream. Now she is a “Reign Maker” for the company’s “Let Them Reign” campaign. She is the first female college athlete to partner with the brand. As explained by the CEO of World’s Finest Chocolate , Eddie Opler, in a press release: “Let Them Reign” was created to celebrate the ambition behind fundraising and the experiences it can help make possible. Having Malia join us as our first female NIL partner marks an important chapter for the campaign. We’re proud to have her represent what can happen when determination, opportunity, and support come together. The campaign focuses on encouraging youth to develop confidence, communication skills, resilience and entrepreneurial thinking while selling the chocolate. Samuels herself used her childhood experience with World’s Finest Chocolates to break out of her shell and improve her communication skills. The basketball it allowed her to play led to her becoming the No. 1 recruit from her home state of Washington in 2023. In high school in Seattle, she won two state championships and received the 3A Washington State Player of the Year award as a junior in 2022. After three years at USC, she is excited to suit up for the Hoosiers in 2026-27. Samuels took the time to speak with Swish Appeal about the deal. Back when you were in third to fifth grade, was it gratifying to know that you were in control and that your hard work selling chocolate was allowing you to play travel basketball? Yeah for sure, it was definitely gratifying, kind of to help my parents out. And I think it was more so fun for me to do than thinking about, “Oh I have to do this to play travel basketball.” It was just something that me and my teammates would kind of try to compete and see who could sell the most chocolate and stuff like that. But looking back, it was definitely gratifying. And now that you’re a Division I college basketball player and basketball is such a huge part of your life, do you look back with extra gratitude toward World’s Finest Chocolate for getting you started on this path? Indiana women’s basketball player Malia Samuels’ new NIL deal with World’s Finest Chocolate is one of those feel-good stories of giving back. She is the first female college athlete to partner with the brand. As explained by the CEO of World’s Finest Chocolate , Eddie Opler, in a press release: “Let Them Reign” was created to celebrate the ambition behind fundraising and the experiences it can help make possible. Having Malia join us as our first female NIL partner marks an important chapter for the campaign. We’re proud to have her represent what can happen when determination, opportunity, and support come together. After three years at USC, she is excited to suit up for the Hoosiers in 2026-27. Samuels took the time to speak with Swish Appeal about the deal. Back when you were in third to fifth grade, was it gratifying to know that you were in control and that your hard work selling chocolate was allowing you to play travel basketball? Yeah for sure, it was definitely gratifying, kind of to help my parents out. And I think it was more so fun for me to do than thinking about, “Oh I have to do this to play travel basketball.” It was just something that me and my teammates would kind of try to compete and see who could sell the most chocolate and stuff like that. But looking back, it was definitely gratifying. And now that you’re a Division I college basketball player and basketball is such a huge part of your life, do you look back with extra gratitude toward World’s Finest Chocolate for getting you started on this path? Yeah for sure. I think basketball has always been such a big part of my life. And without the travel basketball piece from when I was really young, I wouldn’t be where I’m at now. So I do have a lot of gratitude toward World’s Finest Chocolate for making that happen for me. What does it mean to you to be using NIL for a good cause and one that is so important to you personally? I think I’ve always tried to use my NIL for a good cause, whether that be my camps that I did last year or finding a good cause to give back to my community. Just because the high school that I went to was in a kind of rough area of the city. I want kids to kind of like see themselves in me and want to do this when they get to my age and give back to kids. I want the generations to just keep building on each other and giving back to each other. For you, selling the chocolate helped you improve your communication skills, which is something you need on the court. What does it mean to you to not only be helping give kids opportunities in the moment, but also helping them build skills they’ll need later in life? I think for me, it taught me skills that I didn’t realize were so valuable. Like communication, confidence and resilience. Being ok with some nos because ultimately some nos will lead to some yeses. I think it’s very important to teach kids those skills at such a young age. I think COVID kind of messed that up for some kids and their development. So I think it’s important to really hone in and focus on the fundamental skills that kids need now. Can you speak to the significance of you being the first female athlete to have an NIL deal with World’s Finest Chocolate and what that means for getting more girls involved in sports and giving them the same opportunities as boys? I think it’s super significant, and I think for me it has even more significance because I was on a boys’ basketball team when I did sell chocolate. There weren’t like a ton of girls around playing sports. There weren’t a lot of girls that took basketball seriously at that age. So I had to play with the boys. So it’s super significant for girls to get more opportunities, for women’s basketball to get more popular. Having the opportunity to travel and do all these things with basketball, it kind of shows girls all around the world that, “Oh this is really something.” And that’s kind of my basketball story. Like, “Oh I can go to college and play basketball?” Like, I never knew that. So I think that’s kind of what I want to be for the next generation of girls by doing this.

item.title: Mets’ $17 Million Castoff Sends 5-Word Yankees Message
item.description: Bronx, N.Y.: New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman at press conference at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York on November 4, 2022. (Photo by J. Conrad Williams, Jr./Newsday RM via Getty Images) Newsday via Getty Images The New York Yankees enter the offseason facing important decisions about their pitching staff, with the bullpen among the areas that could look different in 2027. New York has often preferred to develop inexpensive relief options rather than commit major money to established relievers, but that approach could be tested as the organization looks for ways to strengthen its roster. “The Yankees have not paid a reliever at least $10 million a season since 2019, when Zack Britton and Aroldis Chapman signed new deals with the club,” Chris Kirschner noted for The Athletic . “The Yankees have instead opted to find scrapheap arms, turn them into excellent pitchers and then watch them get paid handsomely elsewhere.” That history could make a familiar name worth watching as the Yankees consider their options, particularly after he sent a surprisingly Yankees focused message via his personal social media account. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Trump’s Yankees Ally Going Nowhere After ‘Total Fake News’ Dismissal Update, Per Insider New York Mets Disappointment Sends New York Yankees Message Immediately After Season Ends Former Cy Young Award candidate Frankie Montas has recently been on the outside looking in after a difficult stint with the New York Mets, and his latest Instagram offered a glimpse into his mindset as he works toward the next stage of his career. Montas shared a photo of himself wearing a Yankees hat , accompanying it with the message “zero excuses and hard work. The five-word message comes after a frustrating period for the right-hander, whose time with the Mets never developed as hoped. New York signed him to a two-year, $34 million contract before the 2025 season, expecting him to help stabilize its pitching staff. Instead, injuries limited his availability and effectiveness. “Frankie Montas’ turbulent Mets tenure will end after only nine appearances,” MLB.com’s Anthony DiComo reported last offseason . “The Mets designated Montas for assignment on Tuesday, cutting ties with a player who wasn’t going to be healthy enough to pitch anyway. The move is mostly procedural; Montas underwent Tommy John surgery at the end of the regular season and will miss all of 2026. He subsequently exercised the $17 million player option on his contract.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets Outfielder Cuts Ties With Team Immediately After Season Ends New York Yankees Could Reunite With New York Mets Castoff Montas previously pitched for the Yankees after arriving from the Oakland Athletics at the 2022 trade deadline. Montas shared a photo of himself wearing a Yankees hat , accompanying it with the message “zero excuses and hard work. The five-word message comes after a frustrating period for the right-hander, whose time with the Mets never developed as hoped. New York signed him to a two-year, $34 million contract before the 2025 season, expecting him to help stabilize its pitching staff. Instead, injuries limited his availability and effectiveness. “Frankie Montas’ turbulent Mets tenure will end after only nine appearances,” MLB.com’s Anthony DiComo reported last offseason . “The Mets designated Montas for assignment on Tuesday, cutting ties with a player who wasn’t going to be healthy enough to pitch anyway. Still, with New York evaluating its pitching depth, Montas is a recognizable name to monitor as he works toward a comeback. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Why John Daly claimed he could not even watch the 2004 US Open, ‘it was so embarrassing’
item.description: Photo by TIM SLOAN / AFP via Getty Images John Daly once suggested that he could not even bring himself to watch the US Open at Shinnecock Hills back in 2004 due to the condition of the golf course, as he commented on whether he felt that he had the game to win the event at some stage. The US Open is generally the major which offers the toughest test of the season for the world’s greatest players. Just one of the last seven winners of the event has reached double figures under par. Most recently, Wyndham Clark won the 2026 US Open at Shinnecock Hills on four under. Interestingly, that was the same winning score when the Southampton venue hosted the event more than two decades earlier in 2004. However, that year’s US Open is largely remembered for chaos caused by the conditions. Why John Daly labelled the 2004 US Open an embarrassment Retief Goosen won the event, while Phil Mickelson also ended the week under par. However, those at seven over par for the tournament did well enough to make it into the top 10. At one stage, ground staff were watering the seventh green between groups because players were finding it simply impossible to get their ball to stay on the putting surface. And while John Daly claimed in an interview with Golf Digest the following year that he felt he had the game to win the US Open, he insisted that what happened at Shinnecock became a shambles. “I think so [I can win it]. I didn’t play last year at Shinnecock, which was probably a good thing. I couldn’t even watch it after a while, it was so embarrassing,” he said. “Those are my fellow competitors out there, hitting good shots into a par three like number seven, and they take triple bogey. What about golf? What about skill? I couldn’t watch much last year. Stupid.” John Daly and the US Open never got along Unfortunately for Daly, it would never click for him in the US Open. He won both the PGA Championship and The Open Championship during his incredible career. However, the US Open was the only major he failed to register a top-10 finish at. In fact, his best result was tied for 27th. Daly would play in the 2005 US Open at Pinehurst, and would make the cut. However, that remains his most recent appearance in the event. Meanwhile, Shinnecock Hills has gone on to host two more US Opens.

item.title: Despite not being in NFL, Lamine Yamal has outplayed Justin Herbert and Matthew Stafford at SoFi Stadium
item.description: Credit: Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA/Kiyoshi Mio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 2026 Ballon d’Or contender Lamine Yamal has managed to register more wins at LA’s SoFi Stadium than the two star starting QBs playing in that stadium for the NFL. Justin Herbert and Matthew Stafford entered the 2026 NFL season with big expectations on their shoulders, with Herbert expected to finally emerge as a championship-level QB while Stafford led the preseason title favourites. Despite the hype, both star QBs have somehow been outdone by soccer sensation Yamal , who still holds more wins than both of them in their home stadiums despite not playing there since June. Justin Herbert and Matthew Stafford’s struggles highlighted by Lamine Yamal’s success Yamal played two 2026 FIFA World Cup knockout games in the SoFi Stadium (called Los Angeles Stadium during the World Cup), a 3-0 win over Austria in the Round of 32 and a 2-1 win over Belgium in the quarter-finals. This means Yamal and his other national team teammates are 2-0 in the stadium so far, while the Chargers and Rams look to be in trouble. Stafford’s Rams won their home opener 28-6 against the New York Giants with Stafford playing a crucial role in the win. However, they have since lost to the Buffalo Bills (37-34 OT) and Arizona Cardinals (18-16) on their home field, going 2-4 overall on the season and 1-2 at SoFi. The Chargers have lost every single game this season, starting 0-6, including three losses at their home field. Justin Herbert has struggled mightily, as the Cardinals (26-14), Las Vegas Raiders (26-14), and Denver Broncos (23-17) have all defeated the Chargers at home. Funnily, even the Cardinals have a better record at SoFi Stadium than either the Chargers or Rams, but at least they are an NFL team. Yamal and the Spanish national team come from a different sport, making this statistical aberration stand out even more. item.content:encoded: Credit: Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA/Kiyoshi Mio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 2026 Ballon d’Or contender Lamine Yamal has managed to register more wins at LA’s SoFi Stadium than the two star starting QBs playing in that stadium for the NFL. Justin Herbert and Matthew Stafford entered the 2026 NFL season with big expectations on their shoulders, with Herbert expected to finally emerge as a championship-level QB while Stafford led the preseason title favourites. Despite the hype, both star QBs have somehow been outdone by soccer sensation Yamal , who still holds more wins than both of them in their home stadiums despite not playing there since June. Justin Herbert and Matthew Stafford’s struggles highlighted by Lamine Yamal’s success Yamal played two 2026 FIFA World Cup knockout games in the SoFi Stadium (called Los Angeles Stadium during the World Cup), a 3-0 win over Austria in the Round of 32 and a 2-1 win over Belgium in the quarter-finals. This means Yamal and his other national team teammates are 2-0 in the stadium so far, while the Chargers and Rams look to be in trouble. Stafford’s Rams won their home opener 28-6 against the New York Giants with Stafford playing a crucial role in the win. However, they have since lost to the Buffalo Bills (37-34 OT) and Arizona Cardinals (18-16) on their home field, going 2-4 overall on the season and 1-2 at SoFi. The Chargers have lost every single game this season, starting 0-6, including three losses at their home field. Justin Herbert has struggled mightily, as the Cardinals (26-14), Las Vegas Raiders (26-14), and Denver Broncos (23-17) have all defeated the Chargers at home. Funnily, even the Cardinals have a better record at SoFi Stadium than either the Chargers or Rams, but at least they are an NFL team. Yamal and the Spanish national team come from a different sport, making this statistical aberration stand out even more. item.title: Bayern Munich star Jonathan Tah understands the big challenge Arsenal will present
item.description: (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich defender Jonathan Tah knows that Wednesday’s Champions League showdown against Arsenal will be a serious test, and he has plenty of respect for what Mikel Arteta has built in North London. Speaking to The Times journalist Jonathan Northcroft (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Tah praised Arsenal’s recent progress, highlighting the team’s identity and the difficulty of facing them on the pitch. “Arsenal have been doing great the last years, the way they build this team and this identity. We faced them last year and felt how difficult it was to pl ay against them. And it’s always more interesting if a team has a player you know and want to support,” Tah sai d. Tah, of course, was referencing his old pal from his playing days at Bayer Leverkusen, Kai Havertz. The German international kno ws firsthand how challenging Arsenal can be, with Bayern having experienced their quality in last season’s Champions League campaign. Arsenal have develope d into one of Europe’s most formidable sides under Arteta, combining defensive organization with an increasingly dangerous attacking game. For Bayern Munich, Wednesday’s meet ing represents another opportunity to measure themselves against elite European opposition. Vincent Kompany’s side will need to be sharp in possession, disciplined defensively, and clinical in front of goal if they want to leave London with a positive result. Tah’s final com ment also adds an interesting personal angle to the matchup. Having faced familiar opponents and developed relationships throughout his career, the Bayern defender clearly appreciates the extra motivation that comes with competing against someone he knows and wants to support. However, sentiment will only go so far once the whistle blows. Bayern Munich will have to put that respect aside and deliver a top-level performance against an Arsenal side that has plenty of reasons to believ e it can compete for the biggest prizes in Europe. item.title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the Falcons
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 18: Chicago cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) reacts during the NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons on October 18th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chicago Bears traveled to Atlanta this week to take on the Falcons and imposed their will from start to finish. Here are my top three reasons Chicago won the game. Let’s get to it! 1. Competitive Fire Call it competitive fire, juice, edge, ‘want-to,’ whatever works for you. From the opening kickoff through the closing seconds, the Chicago Bears simply wanted this game more than Atlanta. Despite what many people realize, that matters even at this level. Chicago came out to play in this one, and you could tell it meant something to them in all three phases. I’d be remiss not to mention the masses of Bears fans that traveled to Atlanta for this one too. From the kickoff teams blowing up ball carriers, to the punt team perfectly executing some “Banana Balls” to Caleb Williams igniting the offense on the field or defense on the sidelines, these Bears were going to go down swinging. An encouraging sign after last week’s defeat at Lambeau. Zavier Scott looks like an absolute keeper on this team, and his juice on special teams stands out. Daniel Hardy had himself a game both in the third phase AND on Defense with Montez Sweat out. Noah Sewell made his presence felt as well and the contrast between what Kalif Raymond brings to what his predecessor Olamide Zacchaeus brought is night and day – and that’s only the reserve players! When you have your stars putting forth that same selfless effort to win games (spoiler alert – like the two guys listed below) then you have a fighters chance every week. And when your stars are as talented as they are in Chicago, good things can happen. REALLY good things. I might even call them super. 2. Iceman Caleb heard all the noise, yes. But in my opinion, his biggest motivating factor is and has always been winning ball games as starting quarterback and leading his team to new heights. Well, he made quite the impression Sunday, completing over 80% of his passes with zero turnovers and 1 TD pass, in addition to a career-best mark for consecutive completions with 12 straight complete throws. And that doesn’t count the multiple throw aways he had either. Caleb was on fire. When he is healthy and playing like that, this offense will be hard to stop. Remember, Chicago didn’t even have their RB1B in Kyle Monangai this week either. I said it on Bears Over Beers last week that I hoped he learned from Case Keenum how explosive this offense can be even without him playing Superman in the pocket and not only did he allude to it leading up to this game, but it showed on the field. Chicago has playmakers at each position. All he has to do is get it to them. On Sunday, he did just that with EIGHT players securing at least 2 catches. Caleb

And when your stars are as talented as they are in Chicago, good things can happen. REALLY good things. I might even call them super. 2. Iceman Caleb heard all the noise, yes. But in my opinion, his biggest motivating factor is and has always been winning ball games as starting quarterback and leading his team to new heights. Well, he made quite the impression Sunday, completing over 80% of his passes with zero turnovers and 1 TD pass, in addition to a career-best mark for consecutive completions with 12 straight complete throws. And that doesn’t count the multiple throw aways he had either. Caleb was on fire. When he is healthy and playing like that, this offense will be hard to stop. I said it on Bears Over Beers last week that I hoped he learned from Case Keenum how explosive this offense can be even without him playing Superman in the pocket and not only did he allude to it leading up to this game, but it showed on the field. Chicago has playmakers at each position. All he has to do is get it to them. On Sunday, he did just that with EIGHT players securing at least 2 catches. Caleb is back, people. Cannot wait to see him at home this week against last year’s MVP runner-up and fellow 2024 rookie classman, Drake Maye. Expect fireworks. 3. Spidey Not to be outdone by the epic return of Caleb Williams AKA Iceman, Kyler Gordon AKA “Spider Man” or “Spidey” had arguably the most impressive performance of the afternoon. Easing back into full-time action this week, Spidey played only 16 defensive snaps. In those snaps, he accumulated 4 tackles, 3 sacks, 3 tackles for a loss, 2 forced fumbles, and 2 QB hits. Spider Man is an absolute terror for opposing offenses, and we didn’t really even get to see him in coverage, where he is equally as dangerous. After all he’s been through with the public outcry over missing so much action and reports of tension in the locker room, it was huge to see his performance this week and earn himself a game ball from Ben Johnson postgame. With the struggles this defense has had to start the season, particularly in the secondary, Gordon’s return couldn’t have come at a better time as Chicago has the Patriots, Seahawks, and Buccaneers before the Week 10 BYE – and ALL in Primetime. What about you? What stood out most in your mind when watching The Beloved come away with the win?

item.title: 4 biggest disappointments in NFL after Week 6
item.description: The NFL has been entertaining to watch through the first six weeks, but some disappointing trends deserve more discussion. What is going on in Los Angeles with the Chargers and Rams? Was the NFC East hype dragged out too far? Is Cam Ward a draft bust? Let’s dive in! MORE: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 6 The “Super Team in LA Dec 8, 2024; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) throws against the Buffalo Bills during the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Rams in the offseason; many fans were already gifting them the Super Bowl in August. Now, the team has their backs against the wall with a 2-4 record. They are still a poor special-teams team, but their offense is strong. Their defense is towards the middle of the pack in terms of total EPA. Where does the team go from here? The Rams need to find ways to win these close battles. Matthew Stafford and this offense need to come together and start dominating teams. This team should be violent, but losing to the Arizona Cardinals is a tough look on the 2026 season resume. Cam Ward in Year 2 Oct 4, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward (1) runs with the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Cam Ward was expected to take a jump with the Titans, bringing over Brian Daboll to be their offensive coordinator, drafting Carnell Tate, and adding former Giants WR Wandale Robinson. The team is averaging 14.9 points per game, and it doesn’t seem like this team is going to improve. The offense is ranked 30th in EPA/Play, and they are 29th in EPA/Pass. Does this team find a way to tank for Jerimaeh Smith from Ohio State? MORE: NFL contenders & pretenders after Week 6 The Chargers Offense Sep 27, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) throws in the second half against the Buffalo Bills at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images The Chargers’ offense was getting lots of hype with the addition of Mike McDaniel joining the staff to be their offensive coordinator. Justin Herbert has not looked great, and now the team is considering pivoting to Adam Gase as their new guy. Omarion Hampton was getting some hype because Mike McDaniel is very good with running backs. Jim Harbaugh’s seat is getting hotter and hotter. The team’s schedule is one of the toughest in the NFL, and if they continue to lose, then the Chargers are going to have to consider deciding on a new coach. This is the first time they started 0-6 since 2000, and their quarterback was Jim Harbaugh. The NFC East Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) in action against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The NFC East are winless in the last two weeks,

item.title: Everything Indiana’s Curt Cignetti said ahead of Michigan week, after Ohio State
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Head coach Curt Cignetti of the Indiana Hoosiers looks on during the college football game against the Ohio State Buckeyes on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana. Marsh was ruled out of bounds on the fourth down play. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana football head coach Curt Cignetti addressed the media on Monday for his usual game week press conference following this past Saturday’s 19-15 loss to Ohio State and ahead of this weekend’s game at Michigan. Here’s what he had to say, courtesy of ASAPSports (edited). CIGNETTI: Get ready for Michigan, impressive team, especially on defense. But great effort on Saturday. Great football game. We fell short, plain and simple. Gave great effort. Had our opportunities for sure. In in some ways we beat ourselves, which is uncharacteristic of this football team, but I think we certainly proved we’re capable. We just have to clean up a couple areas and use this setback to learn and grow and come back stronger and better. So really tough opponent this week, Michigan. Made quarterback the second half at Penn State. Gave them a shot in the arm. Scored three second half touchdowns to win the game. Really impressed with their defense. Their quickness, their tenacity, the way they played play in and play out, the way they run to the ball. It’s top flight defense. Offensively they’ve got good running backs. Quarterback came in and played really well. The other quarterback, you know, has a cannon and can run; makes a lot of plays with his legs. So they’ll be feeling pretty good about themselves after that victory. It will be a very physical football game again, our eighth game in a row, so looking forward, not backward, and this will be a very tough challenge. Q : How did you assess Josh Hoover’s performance after watching the film and what did you see from him? CIGNETTI: I thought he made good plays. There are some he would like to have back, some overthrows for sure. Q : When a quarterback is missing, overthrowing, does that tell you anything about maybe what’s kind of the challenge he’s facing, or what was going wrong with him? CIGNETTI: It’s just an accuracy issue. You know, there have been a couple other overthrows in games, so. Made a lot of good plays too, so. Q : Nick and Charlie have been I think two of those most targeted receivers in the conference through whatever number of games this season. Both really talented players. What’s the balance for a quarterback to wanting to really feed guys that are that talented and also maybe not wanting to get overly locked in on one or two receivers? CIGNETTI: Well, it’s not like he goes shopping what I want to pick up at the store today. The play has a certain read progression attached to it versus defenses, and quarterback goes through his progressions. We try to get those guys the ball because they’re our best two playmakers. Q: (On the running game

So they’ll be feeling pretty good about themselves after that victory. It will be a very physical football game again, our eighth game in a row, so looking forward, not backward, and this will be a very tough challenge. Q : How did you assess Josh Hoover’s performance after watching the film and what did you see from him? CIGNETTI: I thought he made good plays. There are some he would like to have back, some overthrows for sure. Q : When a quarterback is missing, overthrowing, does that tell you anything about maybe what’s kind of the challenge he’s facing, or what was going wrong with him? CIGNETTI: It’s just an accuracy issue. You know, there have been a couple other overthrows in games, so. Made a lot of good plays too, so. Q : Nick and Charlie have been I think two of those most targeted receivers in the conference through whatever number of games this season. Both really talented players. What’s the balance for a quarterback to wanting to really feed guys that are that talented and also maybe not wanting to get overly locked in on one or two receivers? CIGNETTI: Well, it’s not like he goes shopping what I want to pick up at the store today. The play has a certain read progression attached to it versus defenses, and quarterback goes through his progressions. We try to get those guys the ball because they’re our best two playmakers. Q: (On the running game) CIGNETTI: Yeah, I mean, teams like Ohio State, Michigan, they don’t give up much rushing yardage. We did have some positive runs. We got into kind of a throw mode. I they we called 46 passes and 26 runs, which is very uncharacteristic of us. So, you know, all starts up front. We all want more consistent production, explosive plays. Haven’t got any explosive plays the last two weeks in the run game. Q : With special teams, the two missed field goals, what did you see from Nico? And in hindsight, do you wish you put Paddy McAteer out there for the long one, or did he show you something early in the season that made you think Nico was the choice there? CIGNETTI: No, you know, that first miss was an uncharacteristic miss. We should have been in the end zone the play before but weren’t. The 55 yarder would’ve been go for it and called the play and they came on defensively and didn’t like the look. So called timeout and decided to kick it. I did think about Paddy. We went into the game 56, Paddy 55, Nico was 55. He hit it right down the middle that would’ve been good from 53, because he’s improved his range. Q : (Regarding Michigan’s quarterbacks and preparing.) CIGNETTI: You can see what you need to see in the second half of Penn State in my opinion, which I watched. You know, I would assume it would be him. Could be two quarterbacks on the field at the same time. That would not surprise me. They did a lot of that at Utah. And the other guy can make plays. So schematically they didn’t change a whole lot in the second half. Q: You guys gave Ohio State a lot of problems with your defense. Is it just a matter of coming together with the reps and playing together this long that you guys have really — what has allowed that to happen? CIGNETTI: The defense rose to the occasion. Hey, let’s face it, it was a big contest and our defense played well, played really well. The entire team played with great effort. We met a lot of our goals. They did spit a few runs, but we gave up a little bit schematically to double cover the receiver and we know that this guy might catch a few more, they may hit a few more runs, but put pressure on the quarterback, which we wanted to do. Then forced catches, and the one big one was an underthrow which we just kind of one of those things. But, you know, we’re really good up front and the coverage was tight. Really proud of the way we played. Held them to field goals when they got down there. Created two turnovers. Set up our first score. I thought it was an outstanding effort and we’re going to need another one this week. Q : (Regarding talking with Nick Marsh since Saturday and playing in Ann Arbor) CURT CIGNETTI: Yeah, right. Well, we got a lot of guys hurting after this game, and that play wasn’t all on Nick. There are three, four things that happened on that play that lead to a break down in execution. So I’ll see Nick tonight in the team meeting. Nick will be fine. He played well. He had one or two plays he would like to have back, but had some pressure on that play in Josh’s face, and Josh’s drop wasn’t exactly corrected and then he punt faked it, so he could have gotten it out a little quicker. But it was definitely a layup. Ann Arbor, no, have not played there. Q : On the offensive line how have you seen them adjust to these Big Ten defensive fronts and what improvements would you like to see them make? CIGNETTI: I thought we protected well. Be nice to get some explosive runs going again, but we did — we had a couple drives where we got some nice runs, and we’re starting to, you know what I mean, and then it became a throw game. Basically we lost the game. Like before you win it you can’t lose it. You look at the second quarter. We had momentum; we’re taking control. We go down there and score, we’d be up 11. We don’t execute something that’s like day one in terms of level of execution required. Have to kick the field goal. Hit the crossbar. Doesn’t happen very often. They go down and score. Big turn of events even first series second half. Completed pass. Strip and fumbles the ball. You know, next time went four for four. They gave us a certain look. We didn’t adjust. Sack, fumble. So those are the kind of mistakes. And then the last play of the game that we normally don’t make that we make. So, you know, I think we were all feeling pretty bad after the game that night I’m sure. I woke up, you know, with kind of a new perspective. We proved that we’re capable. Just got clean up a couple things and get a little better in certain areas, so… Q : Coach, how did you feel like you evaluated your players’ ability to mentally flip from Ohio State to Michigan? Do they need on influence from the coaching staff to get in the right mindset or do you think your leaders did a good enough job? CIGNETTI: I mean, look, this business and what we ask of players is not easy stuff; this is hard. It took a lot of effort. It was a physical game. A lot of guys, yo

item.title: Dejan Kulusevski reveals he is a 'smarter' and 'different man' after ending 526-day injury nightmare in Tottenham victory
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Coventry City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport A new perspective on the game Kulusevski has described himself as a "smarter" and "different man" following his return to competitive action after nearly a year and a half on the sidelines. The winger was introduced in the 86th minute to a standing ovation, marking his first appearance since suffering a devastating knee injury on May 11, 2025. His comeback coincided with Tottenham finally securing their first Premier League victory of the new campaign, as they defeated Coventry City 3-1 . Kulusevski was quick to point out that the time away from the pitch has changed his perspective on the game and his own identity as a professional athlete. "I am so grateful that I had to experience it. Now, I am ready to play football. I see myself as different now. I think that I am a different man. The same guy that wants to play football, but a little bit smarter, so I am happy," Kulusevski told Sky Sports . Spurs star embraces the struggle Spurs star embraces the struggle Reflecting on the psychological and physical toll of his absence, the former Juventus man chose to focus on the personal growth he experienced away from the bright lights of the top flight. He expressed a sense of pride in the resilience required to navigate such a lengthy period without competitive football. His return marks a significant boost for the North London club, who have felt the absence of his direct running and creativity on the flanks. The winger was philosophical about the struggle he had endured over the previous 17 months. "I will tell everyone about the journey. It's been an amazing journey even if it's hard sometimes; hard is beautiful," Kulusevski said. item.content:encoded: Tottenham Hotspur v Coventry City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport A new perspective on the game Kulusevski has described himself as a "smarter" and "different man" following his return to competitive action after nearly a year and a half on the sidelines. The winger was introduced in the 86th minute to a standing ovation, marking his first appearance since suffering a devastating knee injury on May 11, 2025. His comeback coincided with Tottenham finally securing their first Premier League victory of the new campaign, as they defeated Coventry City 3-1 . Kulusevski was quick to point out that the time away from the pitch has changed his perspective on the game and his own identity as a professional athlete. "I am so grateful that I had to experience it. Now, I am ready to play football. I see myself as different now. I think that I am a different man. The same guy that wants to play football, but a little bit smarter, so I am happy," Kulusevski told Sky Sports . Spurs star embraces the struggle Spurs star embraces the struggle Reflecting on the psychological and physical toll of his absence, the former Juventus man chose to focus on the personal growth he experienced away from the bright lights of the top flight. He expressed a sense of pride in the resilience required to navigate such a lengthy period without competitive football. His return marks a significant boost for the North London club, who have felt the absence of his direct running and creativity on the flanks. The winger was philosophical about the struggle he had endured over the previous 17 months. "I will tell everyone about the journey. It's been an amazing journey even if it's hard sometimes; hard is beautiful," Kulusevski said. The long road back to fitness Kulusevski suffered a complex knee injury and extensive cartilage damage during a match against Crystal Palace. item.title: Brentford contact police after rugby ball kicked into stadium
item.description: Brentford contact police after rugby ball kicked into stadium Brentford have contacted the police after a rugby ball was kicked from a nearby rooftop towards the pitch during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Saturday, describing the incident as “dangerous” and “potentially very harmful”. Footage circulating on social media appears to show a man standing on a rooftop near the Gtech Community Stadium kicking the ball towards the pitch, while other people nearby laugh and cheer. A separate clip from inside the ground shows a member of staff removing the rugby ball from the playing area as the match continued. The incident took place during a game that ended in a 2-1 defeat for Brentford, with Alexander Isak scoring a late winner for Liverpool after the visitors came from behind to beat the nine-man hosts. In a statement, Brentford confirmed that the matter had been referred to the police and that the club would support the investigation to identify those responsible. No further details about the individuals involved or any potential arrests have been confirmed in the information available. The unusual incident added to a difficult afternoon for Brentford, who saw both Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt sent off in the second half before Isak's late goal settled the contest. The defeat left the Bees sixth in the Premier League table, one place behind Liverpool, who moved above them with the win.

item.title: Banana Ball returns to T-Mobile Park in 2027: Ticket lottery closes Oct. 31
item.description: CLEMSON, SOUTH CAROLINA - APRIL 26: Savannah Bananas perform a routine during a game against the Party Animals at Memorial Stadium on April 26, 2025 in Clemson, South Carolina. A record-breaking crowd of 80,000 reportedly attended the game, the first of ten Savannah Bananas baseball games to be broadcast this summer by ESPN, and the first of three Banana Ball games to be played in football stadiums. (Photo by Sean Rayford/Getty Images) Sean Rayford Seattle baseball fans have until Oct. 31 to enter the lottery for a chance to catch some Banana Ball at T-Mobile Park, where the Loco Beach Coconuts will take on the Party Animals on April 23 and April 24, 2027. Banana Ball, created by the Savannah Bananas, is a fast-paced style of baseball featuring unique rules, including no bunting, a two-hour time limit, fans catching foul balls for outs, batters stealing first base, and a one-on-one tiebreaker showdown if a game ends tied. Where did Banana Ball come from? The Savannah Bananas, based in Savannah, Georgia, were founded in 2016 as part of the Coastal Plain League. The Coastal Plain League is a collegiate summer baseball league in the southeastern U.S. The league originated in 1937 and was revived in 1997 after several periods of inactivity. The start of something new Fast forward many years, and Banana Ball launched in 2020, a concept created by the Savannah Bananas organization . The team played its first Banana Ball game that year, while it was still a member of the Coastal Plain League. Later in 2020, the Party Animals became the first official rival team. By 2021, Banana Ball played its first games outside of Savannah. In 2022, the Savannah Bananas left the Coastal Plain League to become a full-time Banana Ball team. After a series of nationwide tours, the league introduced four additional teams between 2023 and 2026: the Firefighters, Texas Tailgaters, Loco Beach Coconuts, and Indianapolis Clowns. Banana Ball earned a place in the National Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, N.Y., in 2023. A return to Seattle The Savannah Banana’s first came to Seattle in 2025, KIRO 7 reported . This time the Loco Beach Coconuts and the Party Animals will take the mound in Seattle, in full Banana Ball style. Fans can enter the lottery and find more information here . The deadline is Oct. 31 at 8:59 p.m. This story was originally published on MyNorthwest.com .

item.title: Redmond’s Kristina Liutova reaches Edmond Open final, falls to Sloane Stephens
item.description: Kristina Liutova practices in August of 2026 at the Gorin Tennis Academy in Redmond. (Photo by KIRO Newsradio's Frank Lenzi) KIRO Newsradio's Frank Lenzi Redmond’s Kristina Liutova reached the Edmond Open W100 final in Edmond, Oklahoma on Sunday after returning to action last week for the first time since her first-round U.S. Open loss in September. Liutova, 16, won her first four matches in straight sets before losing Sunday’s final to 2017 U.S. Open champion Sloane Stephens, 3-6, 2-6. Stephens, 33, had not won a title since April 2024. She reached a career-high ranking of No. 3 in 2018 and is now ranked No. 118 following Sunday’s win. Stephens has been working her way back up the tennis rankings after suffering a stress fracture in her right foot in 2025. Earlier in her career, she suffered a similar injury in her left foot. By reaching the Edmond Open final, Liutova climbed six spots in the rankings to No. 110. Kristina Liutova’s Memphis Classic breakthrough Liutova entered the Memphis Classic over the summer ranked No. 229 in the world. She fought through qualifying and won the tournament, becoming the youngest active WTA champion and the first person born in the 2010s to win a tour-level event. It was the first tour-level event she had ever played. Liutova’s mother, Elena Morozova, said her daughter has been competitive since birth. “Even when she played hide-and-seek, she wanted to win every time. Even when she played chess with her dad, she wanted to win every time,” Morozova said. “In everything she was doing, she was trying to win.” On the court, Liutova doesn’t focus on results. Her mentality is to put in the work and let the scoreboard take care of itself — the same mentality as her tennis hero. “My favorite tennis player has always been Rafael Nadal, for his composure, for his hardworking character,” Liutova said. “He’s been through a lot of injuries, and the character is just shown in everything. He is just a great human as well, off the court. Always humble. Just an incredibly inspiring person and player.” Liutova is keeping her overall tennis goals and dreams private for now. But she wants to inspire others and take care of her mom, who has sacrificed so much to get her where she is today. “I want to make sure that she’s happy, and in the future, she has an easy life — a house, a cat — and just watch my matches with no worries and no pressure,” Liutova said. Liutova’s U.S. Open run ends against Zheng Qinwen After Memphis, Liutova won three U.S. Open qualifying matches in New York to reach the main draw . There, she faced 2024 Olympic gold medalist Zheng Qinwen. Liutova couldn’t hold off the veteran, falling 4-6, 6-3, 6-1. item.title: Match Preview: BVB Travel to Baku
item.description: BAKU, AZERBAIJAN - OCTOBER 19: Manager Niko Kovac (BVB) during the training session/press conference on day ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 at Tofig Bahramov Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Baku, Azerbaijan. (Photo by Alexandre Simoes/Borussia Dortmund via Getty Images) It’s another UCL night (evening-ish)! BVB face off against Sabah this evening, travelling to Azerbaijan. If you’re anything like me, you’re probably wondering why a team from Azerbaijan is playing in a tournament run by UEFA, the European footballing body. If you’re like me, you should also go look it up, because apparently a small part of Azerbaijan is indeed in Europe! I did not know that. Welcome then, Sabah, to the UCL! Sabah FC have played in the Azerbaijani top flight since the 2018-2019 season, having been formally created as an organization is September of 2017. They played one season in the second division, and were promoted at the end of that season due to financial and licensing mistakes made by the top flight teams, as described by ESPN here . Now, after a few seasons, they have won the Azerbaijani league, and made it through the UCL knockouts to make their first appearance in Europe’s premier footballing tournament. Dortmund on the other hand are a team from Germany that play in yellow shirts. They are coming off the back of two league draws and a loss the Bodo/Glimt in the UCL. Not a great string of results for a team that started their season with five games undefeated. They will be looking to rebound their form against Sabah and steady the ship. Predicted Lineup Given the team’s recent results, expect Niko Kovac to make no changes. That is his usual approach to a bad string of results—double down. Maybe we will see Joey Veerman come in, as Dortmund should expect to have lots of the ball. Match Prediction I’m not sure here. If you couldn’t tell, I do not know much about Sabah, but I do know Dortmund. I know that Dortmund’s attack is stuttering, and Kovac doesn’t seem to be making any tactical tweaks to fix it. If Sabah hunker down and make attacking difficult for Dortmund, we could be in for another 0-0 or 1-1.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo blasted by former Manchester United boss : ‘He let the team down’
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo blasted by former Manchester United boss : ‘He let the team down’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Manchester United manager Erik Ten Hag has no love lost for Cristiano Ronaldo . A few years ago, before Ronaldo’s transfer to Saudi Arabia’s Al-Nassr, he was with his former club, Manchester United. However, toward the end of his run with “The Red Devils,” things started to get heated between him and Ten Hag. However, their animosity ended with the departure of the duo. Now, years later, Ten Hag has reopened his feud with Ronaldo. The former Manchester United manager shared new details about the tension between the two and how Ronaldo let his team down. Ten Hag assumed control at Old Trafford in the summer of 2022. In his debut season, he secured the English League Cup and later won the FA Cup in 2024, prior to being sacked in October of that year. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Speaking to The Athletic, Ten Hag opened up about his experience with Ronaldo and how the Portuguese player was behind the scenes. “He let the team down, and he let me down too, because we were planning for the season with him in it,” Ten Hag said. “I travelled to Portugal to speak with him about the objectives I was seeking to achieve before taking on the responsibility of managing Manchester United,” he shared. “He is one of the best players in the history of football, and I respected him greatly, but as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and rely on the players I saw as the most suitable for the team,” he explained. In his interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag also discussed the shortcomings and Ronaldo’s failure to reach his training levels. Currently, at 41 years old, Ronaldo is still going strong and has been representing both Al-Nassr and the Portuguese team.

item.title: Vikings Trade Deadline Targets: Buckner, Taylor, Bynum & More
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: General manger Nolan Teasley of the Minnesota Vikings looks on before a game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 and reportedly ready to be aggressive at the trade deadline. Who should they target? That’s the question driving the latest episode of The Real Forno Show, where host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano fired up the brand-new A to Z Sports Trade Simulator to break down every realistic target — from DeForest Buckner to Saquon Barkley to Cam Bynum. “If the Vikings want to truly make a Super Bowl run they should make a couple of trades and fortify the roster,” Forness said, pointing to past champions like the 2021 Rams adding Odell Beckham Jr. and the Seahawks acquiring Rashid Shaheed as proof that late-season additions matter. GM Nolan Teasley comes from an aggressive organization and has been calling around. “We’ve heard Nolan Teasley’s calling around,” Forness noted. “All the beat reporters like the Vikings are going to add people.” Key points from the episode: DeForest Buckner is the #1 target. “I think the number one player I wanna bring in of anybody that I think could realistically be available is DeForest Buckner,” Forness said. Beyond the playoff push, he sees Buckner as a developmental mentor for rookie Caleb Banks due to their similar builds (6’6″+, 34-35″ arms) and leverage techniques. Likely cost: a third-round pick plus a token sixth. Justin Herbert doesn’t fit. Despite tantalizing arm talent, Forness has major concerns: “I have concerns that he doesn’t fit this offense.” He questioned whether three first-round picks is worth it for a QB thriving in Sean Payton/Joe Lombardi systems, not Kevin O’Connell’s anticipatory West Coast offense. Quenton Nelson is a risky rental. Stefano noted Nelson is “the fourth-ranked guard in PFF right now” and “a Pro Bowl guard,” but Forness pushed back on spending two thirds for a 30-year-old rental when Donovan Jackson is expected back for the playoffs. Jonathan Taylor carries too much tread. With 2,599 carries since college vs. Jordan Mason’s 859, Forness cautioned: “Tread on the tires matters with running backs. It, we don’t want it to, but it does.” Likely cost: a second-round pick. Cam Bynum reunion makes sense. With Theo Jackson struggling, Forness explained: “This is a PhD level defense where rookies don’t often get a lot of playing time.” Bynum already knows Brian Flores’ system, eliminating the learning curve. Proposed deal: a third, a fifth, and Theo Jackson for Bynum and a fourth. Saquon Barkley is within reach. A third-round pick plus a fifth could land the Eagles star, creating a devastating trio with Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. Pass rush is the priority. “Pass rush, defensive line, I think that should be the priority,” Forness said, noting Jalen Redmond, Andrew Van Ginkel, and Dallas Turner
